q:
I’m standing there trying to do the whole "gentle parenting" thing, you know? I'm validating his feelings and speaking in a calm, soothing voice like I’m some kind of yoga instructor. 

but inside i was just ABSOLUTELY losing it.
cx: Father of a 3-year-old in a floor meltdown in the grocery store's frozen aisle.

q: There was this older couple just staring, and I could tell they were thinking about how a "firm hand" would of fixed the situation in five seconds. Then there was a younger mom who looked like she was judging my tone for not being empathetic enough.
cx: Same father feels judged from both sides at once.

q: You can't just be a parent, you have to be a child psychologist, a negotiator, and a stoic philosopher all at the same time. I’m tired of feeling like my kid’s bad mood is a direct reflection of my failure as a man.
cx: Same father on public tantrums as a performance.

q: He doesn’t play alone, he throws tantrums, he has enough energy for 10 people, and no matter how many books I read, none of it seems to apply to him.
cx: Parent of an almost-2-year-old, three languages, moved countries, few friends with kids.

q: He was in kindergarten 3 times a week (which gave me time to breathe and work on my things) and to play with his peers, since we don’t have many friends with kids ever since we moved countries.
cx: The childcare break ends for August.

q: This weekend we attended our friends’ wedding, and maybe 20 people asked us, “When are you going to have a second?” First of all, rude thing to ask!! Second, NEVER!
cx: What people at a wedding kept asking.

q: My husband can get out of the house sometimes to do things for himself, but I feel like on a very short leash that should jerk me back at any moment if I try to leave.
cx: Mother of a 2.5-year-old and a 15-month-old who screams whenever she leaves.

q: I feel like I'm doing a terrible job as a mother because I'm always stressed because I never have a break […] my husband is frustrated with me always been exhausted and stressed, he wants me to take a break but neither of us know how
cx: Same mother; no break in years and the father cannot settle the younger child.

q: Sometimes he's perfectly fine with my husband watching him, other times not and it largely isn't predictable.
cx: Why she cannot plan time away.

q: Im at the point of getting a new toy every week because he is just bored. We do little to no tv, he eats no sugar or food dyes, organic foods
cx: Stay-at-home mother of an almost-2-year-old who throws, screams and hits each morning.

q: I dont get breaks because im a SAHM and my husband gets home at 7pm. I dont feel like im taking care of myself because im spending every moment keeping him from hurting himself, me, or the dog.
cx: Lost naps were her only break.

q: Its just not always easy because we are on a farm and there are a TON of dangerous stuff for him to get into and he has meltdowns from me pulling him off stuff.
cx: Replying to advice to say yes more and let him explore.

q: I'm at my wits end with my 3.5 yr old boy. He's still no closer to potty training than when we started nearly 10 months ago. I've tried everything I can think of.
cx: Lists ten things tried: undies, naked, pull-ups, timers, treats, praise.

q: We have him on daycare 2 days a week, but they're not great at helping, since their expectations are that he should be potty trained right now.
cx: Daycare expects him trained and does not help.

q: I know we shouldn't compare kids and all, but my first born (boy) was trained by 2.5 and was so easy. I can't help but wonder what I'm doing wrong now?
cx: Second child, unlike the first.

q: We tried being calm. We tried being robotic and not saying anything at all just walking her back. I cried. I begged.
cx: 3.5-year-old screams and gets out of bed for hours since a sibling arrived two months ago.

q: She understands the concept of the rewards chart but any comprehension goes out the window in the middle of the night.
cx: TV and treats removed, M&Ms and a princess-dress chart offered.

q: I tried coaching him to pay attention to what his body is feeling and he just does not seem to understand what I’m talking about. “I see you’re wiggling. What’s your body telling you?” “nOthING”.
cx: Almost-3-year-old trained, then a family death; now never initiates.

q: Realized we were rewarding the wrong thing, and switched up to rewarding him when he does initiate going to the toilet. It’s maybe helped very slightly?
cx: Same parent changed what the sticker reward was for.

q: We’ve tried having timers throughout the day, we’ve tried so many things and I think everyone is just sick of it.
cx: Months of training going backwards.

q: Everyone else had kids (kids museum) and it seemed like everyone was judging us. A 2 hour car ride to spend just 10 minutes at what was supposed to be a few hour event. I feel like such a failure.
cx: Mother of a 3-year-old and nearly-2 twins; the 3-year-old hit both parents at a children's museum.

q: But it feels like a whole new level of public humiliation when your child is the only one having a violent meltdown.
cx: Same mother, writing from the car.

q: I offered my phone (I only did this because I have twins nearly two and one was on my back and my husband was holding our other twin so I was trying to not make a scene.)
cx: Explains why she reached for the phone.

q: I know now in the future to give her a quiet space before going into a new activity when it's a long drive away. We don't live near a lot of toddler friendly spaces so this was supposed to be a fun day.
cx: What she takes from a 108-comment thread.

q: I feel like I’m failing her. We don’t coddle her, yet she’s still so afraid of new things. I see kids half her age jumping off things without a second thought
cx: Mother of a shy, easily frustrated daughter who screams through swim class.

q: We’ve tried everything!! staying poolside, staying where she can see us, leaving entirely.
cx: Same mother on swim class.

q: I’ll keep pushing her to try before stepping in! Maybe I am coddling her more than I think I am
cx: After replies, she wonders if she steps in too early.

q: He has a bunch of emotion regulation books and activities and timers which we set for this. He usually picks the timer he needs but when it's really bad he just throws stuff at us
cx: Parent of a just-4-year-old who spits and lashes out when a switch flips.

q:
Thank you, yeah these are the things I know but just find it so difficult. 

No one tells you how much self work you need to do when you have kids!
cx: Knows the gentle-parenting advice already; doing it is the hard part.

q: He doesn't watch TV but taking away the telly for spitting at me isn't a natural consequence.
cx: Rejects a suggested consequence that does not fit their house.

q: Well I don't know that's why I'm asking for help...
cx: Reply to a commenter asking what she thinks the cause is.

q: It's SO HARD to stay calm, I know it's about modeling behaviour but it's so hard. We've never shouted but internally my body is screaming.
cx: Same parent on staying calm through meltdowns.

q: Wasn’t until she was almost 4 that we started trying again and her daycare teacher didn’t help at all.
cx: Parent who worked at the child's daycare; nearly-4-year-old still poops in underwear.

q: Everyday I’m cleaning 1-3 pairs of poopy underwear. […] with a month left until school starts I’m afraid I’ll be having to go up there and clean her everyday 😥
cx: Pre-K starts in a month and needs her independent.

q: I feel like I’ve exhausted everything. Treats, stickers, ice cream, tech, etc…. Nothing has worked so far.
cx: A T-Rex toy for each potty poop has not worked.

q: I fear her being kicked out if she has too many consistently.
cx: Same parent on pre-K accident rules.

q: I cry hard.. every day .. I cry from guilt, from exhaustion, from the fear that things will get worse and will follow him through puberty..
cx: Parent of an almost-3-year-old with all-day tantrums and a newborn sibling.

q: After he takes his break he’ll come back and we go through the same thing again.. it’s a never ending cycle that goes nowhere.. like I said I’m  literally defeated.. we have NO IDEA how to parent this type of this kid.
cx: Timed warnings and calm-down breaks loop without change.

q: You think we need to be harder on him? Can you give me examples please? I have no idea what authoritative parenting looks like.
cx: Asks a commenter what firmer parenting looks like in practice.

q: oof we’ve tried the sticker chart. He showed absolutely no interest in it. Even when he earned stickers he didn’t care.
cx: Sticker chart did not motivate.

q: I have had NO boundaries. My consequences weren’t consistent. I have let this kid rule the F-ing house! […] These are the best 2 days we’ve had in a while! I don’t want to speak too soon and say I’ve “ fixed” the problems.
cx: Two days later: firmer, consistent time-outs; early improvement after one commenter's advice.

q: Our apartment is all carpet, so no Oh Crap! method unfortunately.
cx: Parent of an almost-3-year-old planning potty training around the flat.

q: we both work full-time and many times we need to leave our LO watching TV while we make dinner and do chores, how do we monitor him during these times? Would the Oh Crap! method actually work in an all carpet apartment?
cx: Questions the method does not answer for their household.

q: Plan: get training undies, a small plastic toilet and a to-go toilet.
cx: The planned shopping list, then weekend training to carry into daycare.

q: He’s literally being so picky I find myself making 2 meals every time it’s mealtime because he’s refusing food. Just overall so whiney. I am exhausted. I feel like I ran a marathon today.
cx: First-time mother of an almost-18-month-old; husband works 12–14-hour days.

q: I’m physically and verbally redirecting him 24/7. Does he give a shit? Not at all 😂
cx: Same mother on redirection.

q: My 3 year old needs to be potty trained to start preschool by 9/1, and we’ve been working on it with her for months. She knows when she needs to go potty but seems to be terrified to sit down on it and let it out.
cx: 3-year-old with newborn twin brothers; preschool deadline in about six weeks.

q: I’m at a loss, bribing her and explaining to her why she needs to go etc aren’t working.
cx: Same parent.
